title: Dimension and the smoothness criterion at the identity of an algebraic group
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $J$ an affine $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $e\in J(F)$ be the identity, and let $T_{J/F,e}$ be its tangent space [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. Write $\dim J$ for its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Both this dimension and $\dim_F T_{J/F,e}$ are finite nonnegative integers, and
$$\dim J\leq\dim_F T_{J/F,e}.$$
Equality holds if and only if $J$ is smooth over $F$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The identity component is not required to be all of $J$, and reducedness of $J$ is not assumed.

source.place: Proposition 1.37, printed p.18, using homogeneity 1.28 and Appendix A.52; dimension paragraph following 1.36, printed p.17.

proof.text: Choose a finite-type affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $e$, as supplied by the definition of locally finite type. The identity section induces an $F$-algebra augmentation $a:A\to F$; it is surjective since $a(c)=c$ for $c\in F$. Thus $\mathfrak q=\ker a$ is maximal and $A/\mathfrak q=F$. The affine-stalk comparison identifies $R=\mathcal O_{J,e}$ with $A_{\mathfrak q}$, with residue field $F$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and itself); finite-type Noetherian permanence and localization permanence therefore make $R$ Noetherian. Write $\mathfrak m$ for its maximal ideal. The group identity dimension theorem applies to this finite-type group without reducedness or smoothness and gives $\dim J=\dim R$.

source.place: Milne Proposition 1.37 and dimension paragraph before it, printed pp.17-18; Stacks Tags 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Apply the fundamental inequality and regularity criterion to the Noetherian local ring $R$: $E=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is a finite-dimensional $F$-space, $\dim R\leq\dim_F E$, and equality is equivalent to regularity of $R$. Apply rational tangent-cotangent duality to $\mathrm{id}_J$ at $e$ to identify $T_{J/F,e}$ with $E^*$. Finite linear duality gives $\dim_F T_{J/F,e}=\dim_F E$ and finite-dimensionality. Together with Step 1 this proves the asserted inequality and shows that equality holds exactly when $R$ is regular. Since $R$ has residue field $F$, its spectrum is nonempty, so $0\leq\dim R$; the finite upper bound makes $\dim J=\dim R$ a finite nonnegative integer as well.

source.place: Milne Appendix A.51-A.52, printed pp.577-578; Stacks Tags 0B2E (lemma-tangent-space-rational-point), 00KU (definition-regular-local and preceding fundamental inequality).

proof.text: Suppose equality holds. Step 2 makes $A_{\mathfrak q}=R$ regular. Its residue field is $F$, a finite separable extension of itself of degree one. Apply the regular-separable affine smooth-neighbourhood theorem to the chart $U$, the finite-type $F$-algebra $A$ and $\mathfrak q$. It supplies an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U\subseteq J$ of $e$ whose structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth.

source.place: Milne Proposition 1.28(b)-(c), printed p.14; Stacks Tags 00TV (lemma-separable-smooth), 00TB (definition-smooth-at-prime), 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize).

proof.text: For every $g\in J(F)$, left translation $L_g$ is an $F$-scheme isomorphism, with inverse $L_{g^{-1}}$ and $L_g(e)=g$. Thus $V_g=L_g(V)$ is an open neighbourhood of $g$ isomorphic over $F$ to $V$, so is smooth by invariance of smoothness under isomorphisms. Let $W=\bigcup_{g\in J(F)}V_g$. Every closed point of $J$ is $F$-rational by the closed-point residue-field theorem, hence belongs to $W$. If the closed subset $Z=J\setminus W$ were nonempty, the Jacobson density theorem applied to $Z$ would give a closed point of $J$ in $Z$, a contradiction. Therefore the $V_g$ cover $J$; smoothness local on the source gives that $J/F$ is smooth. This argument includes every connected component.

source.place: Milne Proposition 1.28(b) implies (a), using homogeneity 1.8, printed pp.9 and 14; Stacks Tags 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize).

proof.text: Conversely suppose $J/F$ is smooth. Restriction to the affine neighbourhood $U$ of Step 1 is smooth. The affine scheme/ring smoothness equivalence makes $A$ a smooth $F$-algebra. The smooth-over-field regular-local theorem then makes $A_{\mathfrak q}=R$ regular. Step 2 gives $\dim J=\dim_F T_{J/F,e}$, completing the equivalence.

source.place: Milne Proposition 1.28(a) implies (c), and Proposition 1.37; Stacks Tags 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field).

proof_origin.place: Proposition 1.37; dimension paragraph before it; Proposition 1.28; Appendix A.51-A.52. Supplemented by Stacks Tags 00FN, 00KU, 0B2E, 00TV, 00TT, 01V6, 0478 and 00FV for the named intermediate results.

lean.statement: theorem tangent_dimension_smoothness (F : Type u) [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (G : Over (Spec (.of F))) [GrpObj G] [IsAffine G.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] : Module.Finite F (schemeTangentSpace F G.left G.hom (onePoint G)) ∧ (∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim G.left = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ topologicalKrullDim G.left ≤ (Module.finrank F (schemeTangentSpace F G.left G.hom (onePoint G)) : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ (topologicalKrullDim G.left = (Module.finrank F (schemeTangentSpace F G.left G.hom (onePoint G)) : WithBot ℕ∞) ↔ Smooth G.hom)
